conviction_note: abs_move 15% (option-implied 15.8%, own median 10.3%, max 23%; $125m cap and a 30%+ short keep it near the straddle) times a p_up of 46: the name has fallen on all 8 of its last prints, including Q2 2026 when revenue beat the guide's high end by $3.8m (+13% vs consensus) and the Q3 guide midpoint came in above consensus, yet it fell 13.4%. Against that, short interest rose to 6.22m shares (about a third of the ~18.4m share class) with 6.9 days to cover, and the options pay for upside (skew -8.4, put/call OI 0.34). Those pull p_up back toward 50. The findings sum to about +0.1 because the small positives (revenue likely in line or slightly above, a known litigation reversal, squeeze potential) offset the negatives (8 of 8 reactions down, financing overhang). The scaled number is slightly negative because the reaction function is the strongest single fact and it outweighs the positioning.
bar: Q3 2026 net revenue. Company guide is about $60-65m (Q2 2026 release, 2026-08-05, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001655210/000165521026000053/ex991pressrelease-q22026ea.htm). Consensus: Benzinga lists $63.9m (Korean mirror $63.7m, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/bynd/earnings-forecasts). In August, LSEG had $62.2m (https://www.foodbusinessmea.com/beyond-meat-sees-stronger-international-demand-lifting-quarterly-revenue-outlook/, 2026-08-10) and StockStory $59.58m (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/bynd/news/earnings-call/5-revealing-analyst-questions-from-beyond-meats-q2-earnings-call, 2026-08-12). I size against about $63.9m, inside the guide. The estimates are dispersed ($59.6-63.9m), so revenue findings are capped small. The bar for adjusted EBITDA and EPS is unsourced. The Q4 2026 guide, which is new information in this print, has no sourced consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest was 6.22m shares as of the 2026-10-15 settlement, with 6.9 days to cover (https://massive.com/quote/bynd, page read 2026-11-04). That is about 34% of the ~18.4m share class implied by Millennium's 13G (957,442 shares = 5.2%, event date 2026-09-21, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1655210/000110465926111444/primary_doc.xml). The trend is rising: 4.3m shares and 5.6 days on 2026-08-19 (https://equibles.com/stocks/bynd/shortinterest), then 5.7m shares and 3.5 days on 2026-09-30 (massive.com / altindex). Some of the short may be hedging by holders of the 7% 2030 converts, which would squeeze less than a directional short. Options (sealed baseline): 25-delta skew -8.43 vol points, so upside is paid; put/call open interest 0.34, so calls dominate; ATM IV 223%; event-implied move 15.81%. Price: -82% from the 52-week high, 13% above the 52-week low, -41% since the first post-split trade near $12.9 on 2026-08-14; run-up +4.2% over 5 days, -3.0% over 20.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue looks headed for roughly $64-65m, in line with or slightly above the $63.9m consensus and in the upper half of the company's $60-65m guide. Applying last year's Q2-to-Q3 channel moves to Q2 2026 gives: US retail $29.6m x 0.87 = $25.8m; international retail flat at about $18.4m; international foodservice flat at about $12.9m; US foodservice down about 4% to $7.7m. The company's guidance record is consistent with this: Q3'25 $70.2m vs a $68-73m guide, Q4'25 $61.6m vs $60-65m, Q1'26 $58.2m vs $57-59m, and Q2'26 $68.8m vs $60-65m, a $3.8m beat over the high end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat consensus revenue by about 10-13% and guided Q3 above consensus, and the stock fell 13.4% over the window (baseline; StockStory 2026-08-12). Q3 2025 revenue came in within its guide and the stock fell 9.0%. A revenue beat has not been bought in any of the last 8 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Consensus at $63.9m already sits in the upper half of the guide, so the market expects roughly this number. Only a second large beat ($67m or more) would be new, and the Q2 beat was driven by international retail (+16.5%), which may not repeat. If the market expected a second large beat, consensus would sit above the guide's high end. It does not.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 channel figures from the Q3 2025 release (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/11/10/3185133/0/en/Beyond-Meat-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results.html). Same company, different document. No independent scanner series for Q3 2026 was found.

findings.finding: Q3 GAAP results should include a one-off credit of about $23.5m from the Sonate/Vegadelphia trademark case. The 10-Q balance sheet carried $38.9m of accrued litigation expense at both 2025-12-31 and 2026-06-27, the full jury verdict of $23.5m plus $15.4m. On 2026-09-18 the court cut actual damages to $37,500 and entered judgment for $15,437,500. That points to roughly a $23.5m reversal inside a quarter whose GAAP operating loss has run about $30m (Q2: -$30.8m, which itself included an $11.0m arbitration credit). The headline GAAP loss could therefore be far smaller than run-rate. Adjusted EBITDA is likely unaffected, and the $15.4m judgment is still a cash outflow unless appealed or bonded.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 GAAP net income was +$16.4m (from a $57.7m debt-extinguishment gain and the $11m arbitration credit) and the stock still fell 13.4%. Q4 2025 had a $548.7m restructuring gain and the stock fell 11.7%. Below-the-line or one-off GAAP gains have not been bought.
findings.why_not_priced: The ruling is public in an 8-K, but EPS consensus on a three-analyst name may not have been reset for the reversal. Any headline GAAP 'beat' would come from this one-off, and the market has looked through such items twice this year. If it were unpriced as positive information, the stock would have moved on 2026-09-22. It did not move visibly.
findings.independence: The accrual figure comes from the Q2 10-Q balance sheet (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1655210/000165521026000055/bynd-20260627.htm). Two company documents, one fact.

findings.finding: Financing overhang. The company can no longer use Form S-3 or its ATM (Q2 release). On 2026-09-23 it exchanged $15.0m of 0% 2027 notes, at 96% of face, for up to 1,945,709 new shares with a floor price of $7.4009; spot is $7.43. That is up to about 10% dilution on the ~18.4m share class. About $14.5m of 2027 notes remain current. The 2030 notes ($208.7m) pay PIK interest, and their indenture was amended on 2026-08-10 to permit further 2027-note exchanges. Q2 cash was $171.4m with debt of $323.8m, and Q3 cash will also reflect the $15.4m judgment if paid. A further exchange or raise announced around the print, as in Q3 2025, is the risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 print came with a proposed new security offering and the stock fell 9.0% over the window (larger multi-day; https://rallies.ai/news/beyond-meat-q3-sales-fall-133-and-december-dilution-fears-trigger-17-drop). The 2025 debt exchange caused drops of 36-58% (2025 reports).
findings.why_not_priced: The September exchange is known and the stock has drifted from about $9 to the $7.40 floor since then, so it is mostly priced. What is not priced is whether a new exchange or registered offering accompanies this print. What the money buys: debt retirement, not a demand ramp. Q2 cash burn was falling (Q1 operating outflow was only $5m), and no going-concern language was seen, so the sign is mildly negative and small.
findings.independence: The S-3/ATM ineligibility comes from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001655210/000165521026000053/ex991pressrelease-q22026ea.htm). The indenture amendment is in the 8-K of 2026-08-10 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1655210/000119312526341312/d156122d8k.htm). All three are company documents, read together as one finding.

findings.finding: Crowded and rising short into the print, with options paying for upside. Short interest was 6.22m shares on 2026-10-15 (about 34% of the ~18.4m share class) with 6.9 days to cover, up from 4.3m shares on 2026-08-19 and 5.7m on 2026-09-30. The baseline skew is -8.43 vol points (upside paid) and put/call open interest is 0.34. The stock sits 13% above its 52-week low after a 41% fall since the split. Any number short of a disaster has a squeeze mechanism on a $125m market cap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest was also high before earlier prints: 27.5% of float per Benzinga's undated page, and about 4.4 days to cover in July 2026. Every one of those prints still fell. The October 2025 meme squeeze came on a non-earnings catalyst (Walmart distribution), not a print.
findings.why_not_priced: The options already price upside (negative skew), so the squeeze is partly in the straddle. The rise in short interest since September means more shares must buy back on any positive surprise. If the market saw no squeeze risk, puts would carry the usual premium on a structurally declining name.
findings.independence: Earlier settlements from equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/bynd/shortinterest). The skew comes from the sealed baseline, a separate source.

findings.finding: This name's reaction function sells its prints. All 8 of the last 8 window moves were negative (median |move| 10.3%, range -4.1% to -23.1%), including Q2 2026, which beat revenue consensus by about 10-13% ($68.8m vs $60.8-62.4m) and guided Q3 above consensus, yet fell 13.4%. This is the base rate any positive revenue fact has to overcome.
findings.why_not_priced: The options lean the other way (upside paid), so the market is not pricing a ninth straight down-move. Part of the drift was pre-split dilution from 2030-note conversions (Q2: 52.1m pre-split shares issued), and those conversions have largely stopped. That weakens the pattern, so the finding is sized below the median move.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline history (SEC 8-K item 2.02 acceptance times) and StockStory's report of the Q2 beat and reaction are independent sources.

findings.finding: Leadership turnover finished in Q3. Interim Chief Transformation Officer John Boken stepped down effective 2026-10-07, and the new COO Brijesh Krishnaswamy went full-time on 2026-09-30, taking over Boken's duties. This may mark the end of the restructuring phase and its consulting cost.
findings.why_not_priced: Public 8-K and unlikely to move the stock. If the call quantifies lower transformation spend, it would show up in opex.

findings.finding: New products and distribution since the last call: the 'Phytosphere' launch of protein powders and bars on 2026-09-09, the Beyond Steak Filet rolling out nationwide at Sprouts (500+ stores) around 2026-10-29 after Wegmans, H-E-B and Meijer, and Beyond Immerse drinks expanding to Southern California and Erewhon in August. Q3 revenue contribution is likely small, but this gives management growth material for the Q4 guide and the narrative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 call (protein-drink launch, Big Geyser New York deal) was followed by a 14.1% fall. Product narrative has not offset the core decline.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-29 (per aggregator; Sprouts release date not confirmed on page)
findings.why_not_priced: These are public press releases. They are unquantified, and the company gave no sales figures (goldesel.de). They would matter only if the Q4 guide credits them.
findings.independence: Phytosphere launch (https://www.fooddive.com/news/beyond-new-protein-bars-poweders-plant-based/829554/); Immerse in Southern California (https://www.beveragedaily.com/Article/2026/08/24/beyond-accelerates-plant-protein-strategy-with-beyond-immerse-retail-expansion/).

findings.finding: Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance was regained on 2026-08-28, after 10 consecutive closes at or above $1 following the 1-for-30 reverse split. This removes the delisting overhang that hung over the Q1 and Q2 prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two 2026 prints with the delisting overhang (May and August) fell 14.1% and 13.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it was announced in September and the stock fell afterwards anyway. Kept as a small structural difference from the earlier prints.

Either party may appeal the $15.44m Sonate judgment. Appeal timing is after the window.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The upside-paid skew and rising crowded short point up, the eight straight negative reactions point down, and the revenue evidence is in line, so the scaled number is a small negative pulled toward 50 by the positioning.
lessons_applied: Rules 1 and 6: the revenue finding lands inside the company's guide on a name that sells its beats, so it moved from +0.5 to +0.2
Rule 2: the litigation reversal is a one-off with no path to the guide, and GAAP one-offs were looked through twice this year, so it moved from +0.3 to +0.2

Rule 4: the financing finding was checked for what the money buys (debt retirement, not a ramp); no going-concern language was seen; and Rule 7 (crowded short) shrinks negatives. It moved from -0.8 to -0.6
Rule 7: the 34% short interest with 6.9 days to cover shrinks the reaction-history negative from -1.5 to -1.0 and moves p_up from 45 to 46
Rule 6: the bar is the company guide plus a dispersed consensus ($59.6-63.9m), so revenue findings stay capped small; unchanged beyond the above
Positioning, leadership, product and Nasdaq findings left standing
